To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(i) the liver is a complex organ composed of many cell types and (ii) the pancreas is a complex organ that is also composed of many cell type.
the pancreas can be a source of hepatocytes and that the differentiation process of stem cells into hepatocytes is a complex process that requires further investigation.

1) Embryonic stem cells can differentiate into cells of the liver lineage, 2) Hepatocytes can be differentiated from adult stem cells, 3) Hepatocyte like cells can be differentiated from pancreatic stem cells, and 4) Hepatocyte-like cells from the pancreas can be transplanted and function in the liver.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of alternative cell sources for transplantation in liver disease.

the identification of the factors that control the development of liver and pancreas and the application of this knowledge to the production of hepatocytes from embryonic stem cells and from other sources.
the generation of hepatocyte-like cells for use in cell transplantation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the most appropriate source of hepatocytes for clinical application would be the use of human embryonic stem cells, which have the capacity to generate hepatocytes and are not limited by the availability of donors.
there is a great deal of research being undertaken to find alternative sources of hepatocytes, but at the present time there are no sources of hepatocytes that are ready for clinical application.
there is no one source of hepatocytes that is ideal for hepatocyte transplantation, but that the most appropriate source of hepatocytes for a given patient will depend on the disease being treated.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is a lot to do in the field of stem cell biology and hepatocyte transplantation.

the development of a cell line with the capacity to differentiate into a hepatocyte-like cell would be an ideal source of donor cells for transplantation, and that stem cell research has the potential to generate a cell line with this capacity.
the differentiation of stem and progenitor cells towards a hepatic phenotype is a promising alternative source of hepatocytes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
hepatocyte transplantation has the potential to become a viable alternative to whole organ transplantation for the treatment for acute liver failure, chronic liver disease, and metabolic diseases.
there are many potential sources of hepatocytes and that these cells can be used for transplantation.
there is no one cell type that will fulfill all the criteria for the treatment of all forms of liver diseases.
